event.title: fix(release): backport clean-pull verification to 0.1.0 RC
event.notes:
## Summary

Fresh runners can share a Docker daemon ID, which stopped release image verification before the registry pull. Check that the candidate image is absent before pulling it, then record that evidence for publication. Keep existing verification receipts compatible.

Backport of #258 to `release/0.1.0-rc`.

(cherry picked from commit 2705d387c0ce6f35b004cd94412fdf35991c0da7)

## Testing

- `bash tests/release/publication.sh --docker`
- `make check-shell`
- `bash tools/release/check-maintenance.sh --event <pr-event.json> --repo .`
- `git diff origin/release/0.1.0-rc --check`

The Docker suite uses a local registry and synthetic release fixtures. Native Linux amd64 qualification runs in CI.

## Compatibility

No breaking changes. Existing verification receipts remain valid.

event.title: chore(release): prepare 0.1.0
event.notes:
## Summary

kgcache 0.1.0 is the first regular release of the standalone string-cache service.
It provides a tested subset of Redis RESP2 and RESP3 for local services and cache workloads.

## Highlights

- Binary-safe string keys and values, conditional SET, expiration, and logical databases.
- Persistent TCP connections, ordered pipelines, and HELLO protocol switching.
- Tested go-redis v9.22.0/v9.23.0 and node-redis 6.2.0/6.2.1, including default RESP3 and explicit RESP2/RESP3.
- CLIENT SETINFO library labels and the documented 22-field CLIENT INFO/LIST reports.
- Snapshots, append-only persistence, recovery checks, and clean shutdown/restart coverage.
- A non-root Linux amd64 image, persistent storage, a built-in PING health check, and Compose examples.
- Rewritten getting-started, application, operation, command, and contributor documentation.

## Try it

```sh
docker run --detach --rm --name kgcache --platform linux/amd64 \
  --publish 127.0.0.1:6379:6379 --volume kgcache-data:/data \
  --stop-timeout 30 kgxlabs/kgcache:0.1.0
redis-cli SET greeting hello
redis-cli GET greeting
```

The replies are `OK` and `hello`. Stop the example with `docker stop kgcache`.
The named volume retains its data. Arm64 hosts need amd64 emulation.

## Compatibility and limits

kgcache remains experimental and supports string-cache workloads within its documented contract.
Authentication, TLS, eviction, replication, clustering, transactions, scripting, pub/sub, and client-side caching are unsupported.
Keep the listener on a trusted network.

Snapshot and AOF restart paths are tested. `everysec` is not a hard one-second loss bound.
Child shutdown polling has a shared budget, not a deadline for all cleanup.
Directory fsync and the broader persistence child-safety/source-error work remain documented limits.

- [Compatibility and exact tested clients](https://github.com/kgxlabs/kgcache/blob/v0.1.0/docs/reference/compatibility.md)
- [Persistence guarantees and limits](https://github.com/kgxlabs/kgcache/blob/v0.1.0/docs/operate/persistence.md)
- [Documentation](https://github.com/kgxlabs/kgcache/blob/v0.1.0/docs/README.md)

## Release preparation and validation

This release request starts from merged main `beddff748374fa9e8539766f8c693bab629f5825`.
The preparation commit changes only image examples and release links from rc.2 to 0.1.0.
Application code, dependencies, workflow definitions, and protection settings are unchanged.

Zig formatting, local documentation links/anchors, and commit-message checks passed.
Required PR checks must pass before the release merge. The publisher then qualifies
the exact 0.1.0 artifact and image on native Linux amd64, verifies a fresh-runner
transfer and a clean registry pull, and publishes fixed references and evidence assets.

event.title: fix(release): backport version progression to 0.1.0
event.notes:
## Summary

Backport #269 to `release/0.1.0`. Each new merged PR reserves the next stable patch or RC number while retries keep their original versions. A tagged older release with a missing bundle no longer blocks a fresh candidate for the next version.

With the existing `0.1.0` reservation, merging this PR requests `0.1.1` and runs native qualification for its new source and image.

(cherry picked from commit a2c3752468cc3a8f87a6fb5d77d7d7a763ee2681)

The cherry-pick applied without conflicts. The PR also updates the maintenance
workflow to use trusted main version rules from #269. This avoids rejecting the
existing `v0.1.0` tag before the next patch can be reserved. The same CI adjustment
is proposed for main in #271.

## Testing

- `bash tests/release/publication.sh --docker`
- `bash tests/release/publication.sh`
- `bash tests/release/maintenance-workflow.sh`
- `bash tests/release/candidates.sh`
- `bash tests/release/github.sh`
- `bash tests/release/proposals.sh`
- `make check-shell`
- `bash tools/release/check-maintenance.sh --event <pr-event.json> --repo .`
- `git diff origin/release/0.1.0 --check`

The full Docker suite passed for the version backport. The CI-only adjustment
also passed its regression test, shell checks, and actionlint 1.7.12. The
publication suite also passed with the new preflight included. Maintenance
compatibility now passes in GitHub.

The Docker publication suite uses a loopback registry and synthetic releases. Native application qualification runs in CI.

## Compatibility

Existing reservations, tags, image digests, and retry notes keep their identities. Stable branches advance patch versions. Both RC branch forms advance RC numbers. RCs keep stable aliases unchanged.
